title: Refactor Zephyr L2 to use async LoRa API (interrupt-driven RX/TX)
description:
Replace polling rx_thread with lora_recv_async() callback. Replace blocking lora_send() with lora_send_async(). Wire CAD to CadDone interrupt.

## Current (bad)
- rx_thread loops calling blocking lora_recv() with 10ms yield sleeps
- TX blocks in lora_send()
- Retries use k_sleep() delays

## Target (good)
- lora_recv_async() registers callback, fires on DIO1 RX_DONE IRQ
- lora_send_async() with TX_DONE callback
- CAD_DONE IRQ drives CSMA state machine directly
- No polling, no sleeps, no retries - just state + interrupts

## Files
- lichen/subsys/lichen/l2/lora_l2_rx.c (rx_thread -> async callback)
- lichen/subsys/lichen/l2/lora_l2_tx.c (blocking send -> async)
- lichen/subsys/lichen/link/csma.c (wire to CAD IRQ)

## Verification
- Existing tests pass
- No k_sleep in hot paths
- Radio state machine matches SX126x datasheet section 13
notes:
Scope: Zephyr C only (Rust Embassy and Python asyncio already event-driven).

Why P1:
- Power: CPU sleeps between interrupts vs spinning in poll loops. Critical for battery nodes.
- Responsiveness: UI/shell not blocked waiting on radio timeouts. 
- Correctness: No timing assumptions. Hardware tells you when it's ready.
- Debuggability: State machine with clear transitions vs "add another sleep."
close_reason: Decomposed into 4 P1 children (async driver API already exists in all 3 drivers, so no driver-exposure child needed; L2 refactor is ~1450 lines across rx/tx/cad + lifecycle, well over 50-line implement threshold): project-LICHEN-worker6-sb0b (RX async: rx_thread->lora_recv_async, immediately ready), project-LICHEN-worker6-0lm8 (TX async: lora_send->lora_send_async + TX_DONE completion, blocked by sb0b), project-LICHEN-worker6-uwip (CAD: blocking lichen_lora_cad_run -> CadDone IRQ driving csma.c state machine, blocked by 0lm8), project-LICHEN-worker6-rx2w (integration sweep: no k_sleep hot paths, SX126x datasheet 13 conformance, full test run, blocked by sb0b+0lm8+uwip).
